issues.label: Sufficiency under Jackson v. Virginia
issues.why: Court must determine whether evidence viewed favorably to verdict allows rational jury to find malice murder beyond reasonable doubt.

issues.label: Circumstantial evidence excludes reasonable hypotheses
issues.why: Conviction rests largely on circumstantial evidence, requiring exclusion of every reasonable hypothesis except guilt, including the burglary theory.

issues.label: Proof of malice aforethought
issues.why: Malice murder requires the deliberate intention to kill, which must be established from the evidence.

issues.label: Identity of the perpetrator
issues.why: Court must assess whether evidence sufficiently identified Sheffield as the shooter given other people present near the scene.

issues.label: Motive evidence sufficiency and weight
issues.why: The affair-based motive theory must be evaluated for its adequacy to support the inference of guilt.

issues.label: Barker v. Wingo speedy-trial analysis
issues.why: Constitutional speedy-trial claim requires application of the four-factor balancing test.

issues.label: Length of delay presumptive prejudice
issues.why: Nearly six years to arrest and further delay to trial triggers threshold inquiry into presumptive prejudice.

issues.label: Reasons for the delay
issues.why: Court must weigh whether investigative and other delays are attributable to the State and their justification.

issues.label: Defendant's assertion of the right
issues.why: Timing and manner of Sheffield's demand for speedy trial affects the balancing.

issues.label: Prejudice to the defense
issues.why: Court must evaluate actual prejudice including impaired defense from delay and faded memories.

issues.label: Standard of review for speedy-trial ruling
issues.why: Whether trial court abused discretion in weighing Barker factors governs the appellate assessment.

issues.label: Pre-indictment versus post-indictment delay
issues.why: Constitutional speedy-trial protections generally attach at arrest/indictment, affecting which delay counts.

issues.label: Admissibility of Stephens affair evidence
issues.why: Extramarital-affair and photograph evidence may implicate other-acts/prejudice rules relevant to conviction's validity.

issues.label: Relevance of stale photographs and phone
issues.why: Sexual photographs from 2009-2010 on unused phone raise relevance and prejudice concerns.

issues.label: Consciousness of guilt inferences
issues.why: Sheffield's demeanor and failure to ask about Edith may support guilt inferences the court must weigh.

issues.label: Accelerant and arson inference
issues.why: Evidence of accelerant use and gas can availability supports the inference of intentional concealment.

issues.label: Weight of exculpatory circumstances
issues.why: Intact jewelry, purse with cash, straws in hand, and unknown persons present bear on reasonable doubt.

issues.label: Preservation of other claims
issues.why: Court must determine whether Sheffield's additional new-trial claims were properly raised and preserved for review.

issues.label: General grounds / thirteenth juror
issues.why: Trial court's discretionary weight-of-evidence review under motion for new trial may need consideration.
